newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds ease, focus on U.S. and UK auctions.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds ease, focus on U.S. and UK auctions.

text.p: Irish government bonds eased in thin late trade on Wednesday in line with Europe as the market awaited auctions in the U.S. and in the UK, dealers said.

U.S. Treasuries were unchanged to slightly higher at mid-morning ahead of Wednesday's $12.5 billion auction in five-year notes while Thursday sees the UK auction 1.5 billion stg of the eight percent due 2015.
"The Irish market kept pace with the UK and Germany while they strengthened a bit this morning but European markets have come back a bit this afternoon and so have we," one dealer said.
By 1440 GMT, the eight percent bond due 2000 had eased 15p from Tuesday's close to 106.75 to yield 5.95 percent.
The eight percent bond due 2006 had eased 10p from the close to 107.70 to yield 6.77 percent.
Looking further ahead, the market awaits the release of economic data from the U.S. on Friday. U.S. September durable goods data is forecast to rise by two percent.
